data.gender_notes: Cassiel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Cassiel is derived from the Hebrew word 'kasshel' which means 'to call upon God'. In Christian tradition, Cassiel is considered an angel who helps people in times of need. The name is mentioned in various Christian texts, including the 'Pseudo-Cyprian' and the 'Pseudo-Benedictine' works. The name Cassiel carries the meaning “Angel of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Cassiel usually hope their child will grow to embody angel of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Cassiel, an angel of wisdom and intelligence, represents deep contemplation and understanding. His name symbolizes the quest for knowledge and the illumination of the divine mind.

historical_references.reference: Cassiel is mentioned in the Hebrew mystical text, Sefer Raziel HaMalakh, which was translated into Latin as 'Razielis Angelorum' around the 13th century. In this text, Cassiel is described as the Angel of Wisdom and Knowledge.

The name Cassiel is also found in Christian demonology, where he is listed as a high-ranking demon, often appearing as an evil counterpart to the Angel of Wisdom. This usage can be traced back to the 16th century.
